extracted.intended_audience: newspaper sports reporters and journalism students
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for reporting and writing game stories across multiple sports (baseball, football, basketball, track, golf, tennis), including what facts, statistics, structure, and techniques to include for clear, accurate, and interesting newspaper accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation lineup and score placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the regulation style of indicating the lineup and the score at the end of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the lineup and the official score (box/line score) at the end of the article in the standard format used by newspapers (as illustrated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a full box score/statistical summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the standard statistical details (batting order/positions, AB, R, H, PO, A, totals) and game facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include errors, two-base hits, stolen bases, double plays, left on bases, first base on errors, bases on balls off each pitcher, hits and earned runs off each pitcher, hit by pitcher, strikeouts by pitcher, umpires, and time of game — i.e., the complete set of box-score/statistics items shown in the example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong, effective lead
rubrics_metrics.description: Open with a lead that captures interest and sets the tone of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good lead (example: unusually good lead in the baseball story) draws the reader in; it should introduce the main fact or hook and invite the reader into the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of expression and selection of incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Use original expression and choose individual incidents that add interest and color to the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond the facts and stats, the writer's choice of striking incidents and fresh phrasing greatly enhances the story's appeal; include telling anecdotes or moments that illustrate the contest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Center interest on a human hero or focal character
rubrics_metrics.description: Center the reader's interest upon a key player (the 'hero') to give the article unity and narrative focus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shift attention from play-by-play and crowd details to the performance and personality of a standout player (as with Oliphant); this can give the piece an almost short-story unity of impression. Be careful to make transitions smooth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smooth shift of focus (avoid abrupt transitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make transitions between crowd/game description and human-interest focus smooth and controlled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The example praises centering on a hero but notes a somewhat rough shift in one story; avoid jarring changes of viewpoint or topic—work transitions so the reader follows the change of emphasis naturally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chronological play-by-play (Game Play by Play)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a clear, chronological account of the game's key plays and sequence of events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include times, sequence of possessions, key plays (e.g., toss, kickoff, punts, critical runs or plays), and short descriptions of how scoring sequences developed so readers can follow the flow of the contest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Getting players' names: use numbers and lineup mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify players by number during play to make taking notes easier, and map numbers to names using the regulation lineup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On teams that wear numerals, follow players by number; on smaller teams without numbers, number positions according to the regulation lineup (sample mapping provided). Take shorthand running notes with numbers and fill in names after the game.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seat placement and access to scorer/insiders
rubrics_metrics.description: To record plays and identify scorers accurately, position yourself close to the scorer or between reliable informants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In basketball and similar fast-shifting sports, have a seat next to the scorer or between students/friends of the players so you can get players' names instantly when baskets, errors, or plays occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basketball: report quarter-by-quarter exact scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Because basketball scores run high and standings shift rapidly, give the exact score of each team at the end of every quarter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the score at the end of each quarter in the detailed account; also include line-up/positions and a final totals table as in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track meet reporting: include event summaries and records
rubrics_metrics.description: List results for each event with winners, times/distances, team placings, team averages, and note any records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track events are announced to the grandstand, so supply concise summaries (winner, team, time/distance), team scoring (points), and highlight new records or notable performances; a summary table for events is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Golf: full summary then hole-by-hole detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead with a fairly full summary (results, character of play, weather, condition of links, competitor notes), then follow with detailed hole-by-hole reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the hole-by-hole account, note length, par, relative standing of players on each hole; provide numerical summaries every nine holes and the score-by-hole card as shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tennis: summary by sets and statistical breakdown
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a set-by-set summary (score by sets) and a statistical breakdown (points, games, aces, places, nets, outs, faults).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The set summary is often obtained from the scorer; supplement it with descriptive play (technique, strokes, momentum) and tabulated stats (e.g., aces, nets, outs) to convey match dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear numerical summaries and scorecards
rubrics_metrics.description: Present concise numerical summaries (score-by-quarters, score-by-holes, set scores, cards) to accompany the narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tables/cards at the end or within the story (e.g., 'Cards:', 'Summaries:') to allow readers to scan final scores and statistics quickly; include team/player totals and key stat totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe playing conditions and local color
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the weather, field/court/link conditions, crowd, notable spectators, and local color that affect the game's atmosphere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details such as fog, rain, attendance, appearance of crowd and important spectators (examples: President Wilson, notable women), and how conditions influenced play and spectacle.
